seoTitle: The Rookie Test: Which Rookie Character Are You? (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take The Rookie test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're Nolan, Bradford, Lucy Chen, Lopez, Sergeant Grey, Harper or Jackson West — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the one who started over when everyone said it was too late, the tough mentor who secretly cares, or the ambitious one with something to prove? Answer 12 questions about how you really handle work, pressure and doing the right thing, and find out which Rookie character you are.

characters.name: John Nolan
characters.title: The Second-Chance Rookie
characters.summary: Earnest, determined and never too old to start again. You bet on yourself when nobody else would.
description: Like Nolan, you're not afraid to start over. He walked away from his old life and joined the LAPD in his 40s — the oldest rookie on the force.
You're earnest and principled. Nolan tries to do the right thing, even when it makes his life harder.
People doubt you at first. You prove them wrong by showing up, day after day.
characters.flaw: You overthink, and you can't leave a problem alone.
characters.signature: A rookie badge, a calm smile and a question nobody else thought to ask.
characters.clashReason: they'd question every rule you follow

characters.name: Tim Bradford
characters.title: The Tough-Love Training Officer
characters.summary: Strict, sharp and scarier than you mean to be. You push people hard because you want them to survive.
description: Like Tim, you're tough. He's the training officer rookies dread — harsh, demanding and never satisfied.
But the toughness has a reason. You've seen what happens when people aren't ready, and you refuse to let that happen on your watch.
Underneath the armour, you care deeply — and the right person gets to see it.
characters.flaw: You keep your walls up so high that people think you don't care.
characters.signature: Aviator sunglasses, a stern look and a rookie doing push-ups.
characters.clashReason: they'd push you harder than you want to be pushed

characters.name: Lucy Chen
characters.title: The Ambitious Rising Star
characters.summary: Smart, driven and fearless. You want to be the best — and you're willing to work for it.
description: Like Lucy, you're ambitious. She came into the job with a clear plan and a lot to prove.
You're resourceful and brave. Lucy took on some of the riskiest assignments in the precinct, including undercover work.
You're a great friend with a sharp sense of humour, and you hold your own against anyone — even your training officer.
characters.flaw: You take on too much, too fast, and hide it when you're struggling.
characters.signature: A plan, a backup plan and the last word in an argument with Bradford.

characters.name: Angela Lopez
characters.title: The Unstoppable Force
characters.summary: Confident, fierce and ambitious. You know exactly what you want — and you go and get it.
description: Like Angela, you're driven. She went from training officer to detective and never lost her edge.
You're confident and blunt. You don't waste time, and you're not afraid of anyone.
You're fiercely protective of your family, and you fight for them like nothing else matters.
characters.flaw: You want to control everything, including things you can't.
characters.signature: A detective's badge, a sharp comeback and a very determined walk.

characters.name: Wade Grey
characters.title: The Stern Father Figure
characters.summary: Experienced, principled and not easily impressed. You hold people to high standards — because you believe in them.
description: Like Sergeant Grey, you're the one in charge. He's the watch commander, and at first he's openly sceptical of Nolan joining at his age.
You're strict, but fair. You've seen a lot, and you don't give out praise easily.
When someone earns your respect, though, you'll back them all the way.
characters.flaw: You judge people quickly, and it takes a lot to change your mind.
characters.signature: A clipboard, a raised eyebrow and a briefing everyone listens to.
characters.clashReason: they'd do everything by the book

characters.name: Nyla Harper
characters.title: The Street-Smart Veteran
characters.summary: Tough, smart and completely unshakeable. You've been undercover, you've seen everything, and nothing surprises you.
description: Like Harper, you know the streets. Her experience working undercover makes her one of the sharpest cops in the building.
You're direct and a little intimidating. You don't hand-hold, and you expect people to keep up.
But you're a devoted parent and a loyal friend, and your advice is always worth hearing.
characters.flaw: You're hard to get close to.
characters.signature: A calm face in a crisis and a lesson you won't forget.
characters.clashReason: they'd assume the worst about people

characters.name: Jackson West
characters.title: The Idealistic Legacy
characters.summary: Smart, kind and determined to make a difference. You carry big expectations — and you want to change things for the better.
description: Like Jackson, you've got a lot to live up to. His father was a high-ranking LAPD officer, and Jackson felt that pressure every day.
You're idealistic. You believe policing can be fairer, and you push for it.
You doubted yourself at first, but you grew into a cop who stood up for what's right.
characters.flaw: You put too much pressure on yourself.
characters.signature: A pressed uniform, a big smile and a very high bar.

questions.text: Someone new joins your team and is clearly struggling. You...

options.text: Push them hard. They'll thank you later
Give them a straight talking-to, then let them work it out
Make it clear they'll have to earn their place
Quietly help. You remember your own first week

questions.text: Your boss hands you the boring job instead of the exciting one. You...

options.text: Do it perfectly, then ask for the exciting one again
Find something interesting in it that everyone else missed
Get on with it. Every job matters
Make it very clear you're worth more than this

questions.text: A friend is about to make a bad decision. You...

options.text: Tell them bluntly. You don't sugarcoat
Warn them — then back them anyway
Say nothing now, but be there when it goes wrong
Ask them questions until they work it out themselves

questions.text: You're under a lot of stress. You...

options.text: Hide it. Nobody needs to know
Take it out on everyone — then quietly make it up to them later
Stay calm. You've handled far worse
Grab control of something. Anything
Grunt and move on
Pass the credit on to the team
"I know."
Feel relieved. Maybe you're good enough

questions.text: Someone breaks a small rule right in front of you. You...

options.text: Call it out. Rules matter
Let it slide if nobody got hurt
Ask them why they did it
Wonder if the rule is even fair

questions.text: You finally take up a new hobby. It's...

options.text: Woodworking. Quiet, and you're good with your hands
Boxing. You'll be the best in the gym within a month
A book club or a trivia team. It's about the people
Volunteering at a youth centre

questions.text: A whole weekend with no work. You...

options.text: Family time. That's what you work for
Say yes to whatever a friend's planning
Still end up thinking about work
Gym. Then peace and quiet

questions.text: You're thinking about a complete career change later in life. You...

options.text: Do it. It's never too late to start again
Tell anyone else to go for it — but stay where you are
Only with a plan and a promotion already lined up
Worry about what your family would think

questions.text: You see a stranger in trouble on the street. You...

options.text: Step in straight away
Size up the situation first
Take charge and start giving instructions
Help — and check on them again later

questions.text: You're a police officer. On patrol, you pull over an old friend. They've been drinking — not much, but over the limit. You...

options.text: The law is the law. You arrest them
Arrest them, and feel awful about it
Call them a cab and give them a very stern warning
Book them — then pick them up yourself when they're released

questions.text: You're a rookie cop. Your training officer tells you to do something you think is wrong. You...

options.text: Refuse, and explain exactly why
Do it, but make sure they know you disagree
Ask what they're seeing that you're not
Go along with it, then quietly check whether it was even allowed
